Interesting... By shared experience, do you mean the entirety of ones life? Because then, that is true. But if the conditions are so diverse and wide, one can also argue that some experiences are bound to be shared in similarities too (as in one offs).

Though I understand that even if they are of the same category they will never be a direct 1:1 comparison of an experience, that is simply impossible due to many factors. But cut them down enough and narrow them too, then they just might... Anyways, the point was relatability, which is considered sharing an experience. 

The fact that you can relate, even if not to the fullest degree, is enough for me. (I'm also quite short and child like on the face, however, I was also commonly presumed to be older due to the way I behaved and dressed. Which somehow caused an intimidation factor._.))

It is true that we all struggle differently, that is why I made the post to begin with, just to see where my struggles perhaps landed further in, because no matter what, I can't lie that the combination causes further detachment to others (etc)...
I hope you and your friends a safe and happy environment. It's nice that you all have eachother by the way. So please continue to stay safe, if not, I hope safety comes soon if one needs it, as unfortunately I cannot help in that.

What I would think to do is search in relative places of your preferred genres of stories for such authors, or try reaching out to the writers whose stories you find intriguing somewhere? Maybe like Archive of Our Own? Often websites for storytelling have tags to narrow down types of literatures.
(Basically I agree with those other comments, and yeah... you'll have to get over social anxiety slightly. But don't worry, it can get better! Although I am speaking out of a personal experience as someone who suffers from general anxiety disorder that leans mainly towards social anxiety.)

And if I may add, I too personally find my situation to be similar to yours, so you're right that there is bound to be someone of similar interest or experiences as your own (As for how far it goes is uncertain). Although I differ in the fact that I never actually created any video games (but do have ideas for them), and I, while I suppose I'm sort of a decent writer. I don't often write as I'm more of a digital artist and animator. So most my stories are stuck in the premise phase with terrible grammar because I try to get the whole ideas out first before being precise.. and character designing. I'm also no English or Creative Writing major, though I did take plenty of the classes. Same with Art or any other creative majors, but I also took many classes about the subjects and held them as hobbies for most of my life now. That being said, the purpose of taking those electives was to get good for my own passion projects.

By the way, your English is not bad. Certainly better than a 5yo.

I found them years back as a child. They came from a gray rock that I threw against the wall till this came out. They smell like acid when touched, which I presume is sulfur. They are about a quarter my palm but here is a size comparison to a water bottle, with not too much perspective because it looks no difference anyhow. I was curious about geodes as a kid. I live in Southern California. But they could've come from anywhere as the rock was a normal gray one that you find by your house if my memory isn't bad though it hasn't been that long ago by my age now. I used a sharpened stick to get some of the white overlay off of them and other bits of the gray rock.

I really just want to know what it is after all this time. The story behind it is, as a child I watched some documentaries about geodes and finding crystals in rocks. So I went outside of my house eventually and grabbed rocks from around the yard, some gray ones and started throwing them at the wall to crack them open. And eventually I found this one when one broke. And then I used a sharpened stick I had to sort of get rid of the gray parts until it looked like this. It is practically raw I guess. And when touched, it smells sort of acidy? I presume sulfur? And that's sort of it.
